title: H II regions and high-mass starless clump candidates. II. Fragmentation and induced star formation at  0.025 pc scale: an ALMA continuum study
question: Whether the presence of H II regions modifies the core-scale (~0.025 pc) fragmentation and star formation in candidate high-mass starless clumps (HMSCs).

recipe.goal: Combine 12 m and 7 m visibilities and image 1.3 mm continuum
recipe.method: Combine 12 m and 7 m datasets with CASA task CONCAT, regrid single polarization (XX) continuum to 9 MHz channels, and clean line-free channels with TCLEAN (both 12 m + 7 m combined and 7 m alone); estimate recovered flux fraction relative to ATLASGAL 870 um.
key_parameters: cell = 0.3" (combined) and 1" (7 m); robust = 0.5; clean threshold = 0.4 mJy Beam^-1 (combined) and 4 mJy Beam^-1 (7 m); field down to 20% primary beam power point
assumptions: Dust emissivity spectral index beta ~ 1.5 for extrapolating ATLASGAL 870 um flux to 1.3 mm

recipe.goal: Extract dense cores and 7 m ensembles using dendrograms
recipe.method: Run Astrodendrograms on primary beam uncorrected 7 m + 12 m combined continuum images to extract leaves as cores, and on 7 m ACA continuum images to extract larger leaves and classify candidate ensembles (splitting elongated leaves with major/minor > 2.5 by contour peaks/subpeaks and adding weak structures hosting combined cores).
key_parameters: Combined images: min_value = 3 rms, min_delta (step) = 1 rms, min_npix = half of synthesized beam
7 m ACA images: min_value = 2.5 rms, min_delta (step) = 1 rms, min_npix = half of 7 m ACA synthesized beam
assumptions: Leaves in the dendrogram have no substructures and correspond to dense cores; prolonged 7 m leaves (major-to-minor ratio > 2.5) with multiple contour subpeaks represent multiple candidate ensembles sharing the leaf density.

recipe.goal: Derive core and ensemble masses, surface densities, and volume/column densities
recipe.method: Compute core and ensemble masses from primary beam corrected integrated 1.3 mm flux using optically thin isothermal dust emission equation (Eq. 1), and calculate surface density, H2 column density, and H2 number density assuming spherical geometry.
key_parameters: Gas-to-dust ratio R_gd = 100; dust opacity kappa_nu = 0.9 cm^2 g^-1; molecular weight per H2 molecule mu_H2 = 2.8; T_dust = single-dish clump T_dust and T_dust +/- 3 K
assumptions: Optically thin dust continuum emission, spherical core geometry, thin ice mantle dust opacity at density ~10^6 cm^-3 (0.9 cm^2 g^-1), gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100, and combined R_gd/kappa_nu uncertainty of 30%.

recipe.goal: Analyze fragmentation scales using Jeans parameters, Minimum Spanning Tree (MST), and modality tests
recipe.method: Calculate thermal, turbulent (total support), compressible flow, and cylindrical Jeans masses and lengths for clumps and ensembles; measure nearest neighbor separations among cores and ensembles using Minimum Spanning Tree (MST); test modality of scaled core separations combined with literature samples using Hartigan's Dip test and ACR test.
key_parameters: Mean molecular weight per free particle mu = 2.37; molecular weight mu_mole = 29 for 13CO and 30 for C18O and H13CO+; histogram bin sizes = 0.075 and 0.15
assumptions: Average projection factor between projected and actual separation is 2/pi; for cylindrical fragmentation in AS3 and NA3, central density rho_c is assumed to be the minimum density of the cores embedded in the filament.

recipe.goal: Analyze H II region shaping, multi-wavelength profiles, and collect-and-collapse timescale
recipe.method: Compare flux-weighted clump centers (ATLASGAL and Hi-GAL PPMAP) with mass-weighted ALMA core centers; extract intensity and multi-temperature column density profiles along interaction directions; subtract normalized combined 1.3 mm intensity from normalized 20 cm intensity for AS1; fit Gaussian to MALT90 H13CO+ spectrum; calculate collect-and-collapse fragmentation time t_frag for AS1.
key_parameters: Sound speed inside shell for AS1 = 0.24 km s^-1 (C_0.2 = 1.2)
assumptions: 20 cm radio continuum of H II region is optically thin free-free emission; warm dust at 20-30 K is located in the photodissociation region (PDR).
